prompt: When is a metric worth collecting, by this lesson?

choices.text: When it goes up every month on the team dashboard
When it answers a question someone must decide
When it is easy to collect
choices.why: That is how bad metrics start.

choices.text: Always

prompt: Put the steps of the Goal, Question, Metric approach in order.
trap: Most bad metrics come from running it backwards.

prompt: Why is "test cases executed" a poor measure of testing?

choices.text: It is always zero
Testers do not execute tests
choices.why: It is; the count is what misleads.

choices.text: It counts activity, not defects found
choices.why: Right: a hundred trivial cases and one careful one count as a hundred and one.

choices.text: It is hard to count
choices.why: It is easy, which is part of the trouble.

prompt: What do Cine Aurora’s three metrics have in common?

choices.text: They look at what reaches the customer
choices.why: Right: not at how busy the team was.

choices.text: They are all percentages of the defects found
They rank the testers
They can be read on the day of the release, before the customers have seen it

prompt: What does Goodhart’s law say, in Strathern’s phrasing?

choices.text: The money supply should grow at a fixed rate every year to keep prices steady
choices.why: Goodhart was an economist; this is not his law.

choices.text: A measure made a target stops being a good measure
Numbers never lie
choices.why: The law says the opposite about targets.

choices.text: Measure everything

prompt: Match each target to what people reasonably do with it.

pairs.right: downgrade them on the last day

prompt: Most of the damage Goodhart’s law does comes from whom?

choices.text: Honest people
choices.why: Right: the number is what gets improved, by the cheapest route.

choices.text: People who cheat
choices.why: The lesson says it is not mainly cheating.

choices.text: Customers who complain
Managers who never look at the dashboards they asked the team to produce
choices.why: That is theatre, a different point.

prompt: Which are signs of metrics theatre? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: the numbers always go the right way
nobody can say what decision a change led to
producing the report costs more than it saves
a number is dropped after it changes nothing twice

prompt: A team is rewarded for defects found. What happens to the whole-team approach?
hint: Developers become the source of a score.

choices.text: Nothing changes
Developers start writing more tests of their own to protect themselves
It turns into a contest between finders and writers
choices.why: Right: the relationship this course argues against.

choices.text: It grows stronger

prompt: A team found 18 defects before release and customers found 2 after. What is the detection percentage?
In Cine Aurora’s records, how many defects escaped?
Why is the detection percentage hard to game?

choices.text: It is secret
It is read on release day
Nobody on the team knows how to calculate it from the records
Customers report the defects it counts against you
choices.why: Right: those cannot be closed as "won’t fix" on Thursday night.

prompt: Defect 8, the seat map on phones, escaped. Why does the lesson call it the honest kind of escape?

choices.text: The gap was known, written down and accepted
choices.why: Right: it was on the list of things not tested.

choices.text: It was not a real defect
A customer found it quickly, on the first weekend after release
It was fixed in three days by Rafael, which is faster than any other defect in the file
choices.why: Others were fixed faster, and speed is not the point.

prompt: Every month Lia brings three numbers. How is each one shown?

choices.text: As a trend line over the last year
Ranked by tester
Coloured green, amber or red against a target set at the start of the year
choices.why: A target is what this lesson warns about.

choices.text: With the defects behind it

prompt: Which stance does the course end on?

choices.text: Nobody ships without knowing what they ship
choices.why: Right: and the best defects are prevented by an early question.

choices.text: The tester decides every release
Automate everything
Test at the end

prompt: Match each idea to the lesson group it belongs to.
Someone proposes a new number for the dashboard. What does Cine Aurora ask first?
hint: The question this lesson keeps returning to.

choices.text: Which tester will be measured by it, and what bonus does it set for them?
choices.why: Nobody is ranked by numbers here.

choices.text: What decision would change if it changed?
Can it be automated?
Does it look good on the dashboard in the review meeting?
